# refblock-identity-fixtures.txt — committed arms for the REFBLOCK_RE identity scan
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The seven detector constants are declared once, in
# core/hooks/lib/fragile-ref-patterns.sh, and read by every surface listed in that file's
# `Sourced by:` block. cutover-fixtures.txt already proves the PATTERNDECL detector can
# tell a declaration from a line that merely names one. What no fixture proved is the
# property that actually failed in practice: a surface OUTSIDE the runner's hardcoded
# target list declared its own REFBLOCK_RE, the value drifted from the canonical one, and
# nothing measured it — REFBLOCK_RE had zero behavioural coverage, so the scan could only
# assert the constant was SET, never that a copy of it still AGREED.
#
# These are the committed arms for the discovered-population identity scan that closes
# that hole. The scan runs over every tracked shell / YAML / Python / awk file, so the next
# copy is caught wherever it lands rather than only in three named files.
#
# FORMAT (one test case per non-comment line) — the cutover-fixtures.txt schema, verbatim:
#   <EXPECT>\t<CLASS>\t<content>
# where
#   <EXPECT>  = FLAG  (the arm MUST report this site)
#             | CLEAN (the arm MUST NOT report this site)
#   <CLASS>   = REFBLOCK-DECL  | REFBLOCK-SHAPE
#   <content> = "<relpath>|<line content>" — the pipe-delimited idiom ISSUEREF-POS uses.
#               Split on the FIRST '|' (a relative path never contains one); the line
#               content may contain as many more as it likes.
#
# The runner materialises every row as a one-line file at <relpath> under a throwaway
# root, ENUMERATES that root from the filesystem (not from this list), and runs the real
# scan over it. So a row exercises discovery, the path guard, the detector and the value
# comparison together — not just a regex.
#
# THE TWO ARMS ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND CARRY DIFFERENT AUTHORITY.
#   REFBLOCK-DECL  — name-anchored. Finds sites that DECLARE `REFBLOCK_RE`. A site whose
#                    value is byte-identical to the canonical one is accounted for, not
#                    reported: byte-identity is one of the two states the contract allows
#                    (the other being sourcing). A site whose value DIVERGES is a finding
#                    and FAILS the run. Precise, so it is allowed to block.
#   REFBLOCK-SHAPE — value-shaped. Finds the reference-block anchor shape under ANY
#                    variable name, which is what a name-anchored probe structurally
#                    cannot see. It matches on a CONJUNCTION — the heading-level anchor AND
#                    the bracketed spelling — which is also what stops it reporting its own
#                    declaration, since each half is declared on its own line. It
#                    over-includes by construction — an independent surface may legitimately
#                    carry an ancestor of this shape while answering a different question —
#                    so it REPORTS and never fails.
#
# @@CANONICAL@@ expands to the live value of REFBLOCK_RE at run time. It is a sentinel and
# not a literal on purpose: writing the canonical bytes into this file would create a THIRD
# copy of the value, which is the exact defect class the scan exists to prevent. The
# identical-value rows therefore stay correct across any future widening of the canonical
# set, and they test the comparison rather than pinning the value.

# ─── REFBLOCK-DECL — sensitivity: a divergent declaration MUST be reported ────
# Each carries a genuinely different recognized-spelling set, and each uses one of the
# three declaration syntaxes that have appeared in this repo (plain, `readonly`-prefixed,
# and indented inside a YAML block scalar) — a detector that parsed only one of them would
# pass a fixture that tested only one.
FLAG	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/deploy/tools/divergent-plain.sh|REFBLOCK_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Rr]eferences)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
FLAG	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/hooks/divergent-readonly.sh|readonly REFBLOCK_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Pp]rovenance)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
FLAG	REFBLOCK-DECL	.github/workflows/divergent-indented.yml|          REFBLOCK_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Ss]ources?)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'

# ─── REFBLOCK-DECL — specificity: true near-misses that MUST NOT be reported ──
# (a) A byte-identical declaration. It is a redeclaration, but identity holds, so it is
#     accounted for rather than reported — the contract permits byte-identity as well as
#     sourcing, and reporting it would make the arm fire on a state the contract allows.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/deploy/tools/identical-plain.sh|REFBLOCK_RE='@@CANONICAL@@'
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/hooks/identical-readonly.sh|readonly REFBLOCK_RE='@@CANONICAL@@'
# (b) A line that NAMES the constant and declares nothing. It differs from the positives
#     only in the property under test — a declaration anchored at line start — so it is a
#     real near-miss rather than an unrelated line that would pass vacuously.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/deploy/tools/names-only.sh|  REFBLOCK_HIT="$(grep -m1 -nE "$REFBLOCK_RE" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)"
# (c) The ancestor anchor shape under a different variable name. The name arm must stay
#     silent on it; the shape arm below is the one that speaks.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	.github/workflows/decl-ancestor-anchor.yml|            | grep -nE '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+[Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$' \
# (d) THE PATH GUARD, armed. Both rows carry a divergent value that WOULD be reported at
#     any other path, so a zero here measures the guard rather than the content. The
#     canonical library is excluded because it IS the declaration; the fixture directory is
#     excluded because its rows are data, not a consuming surface. Both exclusions are path
#     guards in the scan loop — not entries in an exemption list a later edit could widen.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/hooks/lib/fragile-ref-patterns.sh|REFBLOCK_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Rr]eferences)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-DECL	core/hooks/testdata/decoy-decl-fixtures.txt|REFBLOCK_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Rr]eferences)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'

# ─── REFBLOCK-SHAPE — sensitivity: the shape under any name MUST be reported ──
# This is the arm that sees what a name-anchored probe cannot. The renamed-copy row is the
# live class it exists for: this repo already carries constants re-declared under prefixed
# local names, so a probe searching for the canonical NAME returns zero on them.
FLAG	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	core/deploy/tools/shape-renamed.sh|c99_refblock_re='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Rr]eferences)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
FLAG	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	.github/workflows/shape-ancestor-anchor.yml|            | grep -nE '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+[Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$' \

# ─── REFBLOCK-SHAPE — specificity: near-misses that MUST NOT be reported ──────
# The shape probe is a CONJUNCTION — the heading-level anchor AND the bracketed spelling —
# so these rows split the pair and assert that neither half alone is a copy.
# (a) Anchor without the spelling: a heading anchor of the same GRAMMAR carrying a different
#     heading word. It differs only in the reference-block vocabulary under test.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	core/deploy/tools/shape-absent.sh|CHANGELOG_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+[Cc]hangelog[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
# (a2) Spelling without the anchor: the shape a DETECTOR's own search literal takes. This is
#     the row that keeps the probe from reporting itself — the scan declares this exact
#     fragment, and a probe that flags its own declaration cannot be read.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	core/deploy/tools/shape-spelling-only.sh|SPELLING_FRAGMENT='[Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences'
# (b) Prose naming the recognized headings without carrying the pattern shape — the form
#     the gate's own user-facing failure message and its fixture generator both take.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	core/deploy/tools/shape-prose.sh|  echo "a valid reference must sit under Issue References / References / Related / Provenance / Source / Sources / Source(s)"
# (c) The path guard again, on this arm's own detector.
CLEAN	REFBLOCK-SHAPE	core/hooks/testdata/decoy-shape-fixtures.txt|SOME_RE='^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+([Ii]ssue [Rr]eferences|[Rr]eferences)[[:space:]]*:?[[:space:]]*$'
